title: School group sees alarming rise in violence, bullying
summary: The Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations of the Philippines yesterday warned of an alarming rise in school violence, hooliganism and student-on-student bullying across both public…

blocks.text: At a press conference in Taguig, COCOPEA chairman Irineo Alvaro Jr. said addressing violence and bullying in schools requires more than stricter rules and tighter security measures.

MANILA, Philippines — The Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations of the Philippines (COCOPEA) yesterday warned of an alarming rise in school violence, hooliganism and student-on-student bullying across both public and private schools.
“It requires empowering schools, teachers and officials and parents to instill genuine personal discipline and values formation as part of a long-term solution,” Alvaro said.
He urged all educational institutions to reclaim their constitutional role in character formation with courage and clarity.

“Protecting students from abuse and enforcing firm, fair discipline are not opposites – they go hand in hand. While strictly upholding the ban on corporal punishment and all protections against child abuse, schools must stand firmly behind their teachers, consistently enforce clear behavioral standards and partner closely with parents to teach the value of discipline,” Alvaro added.
When homes and schools fail to teach young people accountability, he said, they risk breeding apathy, violence and corruption in society.
“When educational institutions lead with fair and consistent discipline, we shape learners who value their education and become responsible nation-builders,” Alvaro said.
Ateneo de Davao University and Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP) president Fr. Karel San Juan said schools should make sure there are sufficient guidance counselors.

“There are many reasons for the increase of bullying and school violence incidents. First, a lot of people say that the general culture of violence may be attributed to the general culture of the youth also. The psychology and emotional well-being of our children are very complex. We need to have very strong, updated and improving formation programs to emphasize values like camaraderie, positive behavior, friendship in our campuses,” San Juan said.
He said schools should make sure that student manuals are aligned with the current laws on bullying, child protection and data protection.
